thesis: Franco-Nevada is the world's largest gold-focused royalty and streaming company, giving asset-light exposure to precious metals with no operating cost, capex, or debt risk — H1 2026 delivered record revenue of $1,231.6M (+67%), a 91.1% adjusted EBITDA margin, and $807.5M of adjusted net income ($4.19/share), on top of FY2025 revenue of $1.82B (+64%). The company is debt-free with $1.0B cash and $4.3B of available capital, is tracking toward the upper half of its 510,000-570,000 GEO guidance for 2026, and has H2-weighted production plus first Cobre Panama stockpile stream deliveries ahead. At ~32x trailing earnings the multiple is full, and the main risks are gold's correction to roughly $4,300/oz (below the $4,500/oz guidance assumption) and an unresolved Cobre Panama situation now in the hands of a Panamanian ministerial commission after the company suspended its ICSID arbitration.

financials.fcf: $1.49B operating cash flow (FY2025); $1,002.9M (H1 2026), effectively all free cash flow

drivers: Gold sustains $4,800/oz or higher on central bank and sovereign demand, lifting adjusted EPS toward ~$10.75
GEOs land at the top of the 510,000-570,000 guidance range as Candelaria, Cote Gold, Greenstone, Valentine and Tocantinzinho ramp in H2 2026
Panama's ministerial commission clears a Cobre Panama restart, restoring an asset that once produced ~15% of quarterly revenue and carries no cost to Franco-Nevada
$4.3B of available capital converted into accretive streams and royalties at scale, as with the A$200M Minerals 260 package
Elevated oil and NGL prices keep Diversified revenue above the $245-285M guidance range

base_case.assumptions: Gold averages $4,300-$4,500/oz through 2026-2027 and silver stays below the $75/oz guidance assumption; GEOs land in the upper half of guidance at ~550K; FY2026 revenue ~$2.5B with ~91% adjusted EBITDA margin and adjusted EPS near the ~$8.55 FY2027 consensus; Cobre Panama stockpile deliveries proceed as scheduled (~23,100 gold oz and ~265,000 silver oz in total) but no restart is assumed; the premium multiple holds near 31x forward earnings.

risks: Gold retraces to $3,400-$3,600/oz as long-term yields stay at multi-decade highs, cutting adjusted EPS to roughly $6.25
Premium multiple de-rates from ~32x toward the low 20s, compounding the earnings decline
Panama's ministerial commission rules against a restart and the stockpile programme ends in 2027 with no recovery path, the arbitration having been suspended
Further consensus misses as third-party operators slip — Q2 2026 already missed on both revenue and EPS
Canada Revenue Agency audit exposure or changes to Canadian tax treatment of offshore streams reduce after-tax cash flow

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results — first quarter including Cobre Panama stockpile stream deliveries and H2-weighted production ramp
Cote Gold reserve update and 40,000 tpd expansion study; Copper World sanctioning decision; AurMac final EIS and Record of Decision; Castle Mountain final EIS
Expected annual dividend increase (quarterly dividend was raised 16% to $0.44 in January 2026)
FY2026 results and 2027 guidance, including updated commodity price assumptions and GEO outlook
Panamanian ministerial commission decision on the future of the Cobre Panama mine

key_risks: Cobre Panama unresolved: mine in Preservation and Safe Management since November 2023, ICSID arbitration voluntarily suspended, outcome now dependent on a Panamanian ministerial commission with no deadline
Gold price sensitivity — roughly 70% of revenue is gold and 86% precious metals, with spot below the $4,500/oz guidance assumption
Premium valuation at ~32x trailing earnings is procyclical and de-rates alongside lower metal prices and higher long-term yields
Full dependence on third-party operators for production timing and volumes, with no operational control
Jurisdictional concentration in Latin America (40% of revenue from South America, 7% from Central America and Mexico)
Canada Revenue Agency audit exposure and potential changes to Canadian tax treatment of offshore streams
Capital deployment risk — overpaying for streams in a high gold price environment permanently impairs returns
